relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Solomon binds his new throne to Egypt through a woman whose political marriage helps build palace, temple, and city wall.
Before the central temple, the people's worship remains dispersed across high places.
Love for YHWH coexists with practices the later narrative will judge as incomplete.
Royal devotion appears through a thousand animals consumed at the great sanctuary.
In sleep, power is asked what it truly desires.
Solomon interprets his throne through covenant-kindness shown to David.
He confesses inexperience rather than pretending the crown has made him competent.
The number and complexity of the people exceed one ruler's easy mastery.
He asks not for sharper command but for a heart that listens before judging.
The request pleases the Divine because it is oriented toward responsibility.
Solomon has not asked for longevity, wealth, or enemies' deaths.
Discernment is given as a gift rather than a royal possession earned by status.
Wealth and honor arrive beside wisdom, beginning the tension between discernment and accumulation.
Long life remains conditional upon faithful practice.
The dream returns Solomon to worship and a feast shared with servants.
Two stigmatized women enter the highest court without male sponsors.
One begins with the shared house and the birth of her child.
Their isolation means no external witness can settle the dispute.
One infant has died in the night, and grief stands beneath every accusation.
The first woman alleges a midnight exchange of living and dead children.
Her embodied knowledge recognizes that the dead child is not the one she bore.
Two claims collide without records, witnesses, or institutional protection.
Solomon restates both voices before acting.
A sword enters the courtroom and makes royal danger immediate.
The king proposes an impossible equality that would destroy the child.
One woman chooses the child's life over possession, while the other accepts division.
The threat is withdrawn and the living child returned to the woman whose compassion refused his death.
The nation sees discernment in the judgment, though fear of the ruler accompanies wonder.

contemplative_note: Wisdom begins as a listening heart, especially when those before power are stigmatized, isolated, grieving, and without witnesses. Yet even celebrated wisdom must be questioned when it uses terror as a test.
